format_decision: Single running logbook page, day entries appended as dispatches arrive (the structure question deferred at hub-creation is now decided — matches the Quantum Pacific Coastal logbook precedent, one URL for the week). No placeholder sections for future days (site rule: no coming-soon content).

day_1.source: Ken's in-session dispatch from aboard, verbatim basis: 'embarkation was smooth, rooms are dirty and deteriorated. Toenails on the floor, detritus from previous guests. We're giving them an opportunity to fix it.'
day_1.fidelity_notes: Entry contains ONLY the dispatched facts: smooth embarkation; rooms (plural, as dispatched) dirty and deteriorated; toenails on the floor; detritus from previous guests; opportunity-to-fix posture. Deliberately NOT invented: cabin numbers, deck, times, staff interactions, meals, sailaway, shore-power observations (owed but not yet dispatched — entry defers them to Day 2 explicitly). The 'turnaround day is a hard day for housekeeping' line is general fairness framing, not a claim about this crew.
day_1.pastoral_handling: Failure stated plainly per PASTORAL_GUARDRAILS/never-chipper rule ('There's no soft way to write that sentence, and I'm not going to try'); fairness posture is the operator's own ('the same standard I'd ask readers to hold us to'); no outrage amplification; verdict explicitly deferred to the ship's response.

day_1_evening_addendum.source: Ken's second in-session dispatch from aboard: 5 photos ('Some of the issues') + hot-tub observation verbatim basis: 'they are very unequal in their application of the no drinks in the hot tub rule. People with alcohol - that's fine. People with soda it's not fine. Unsweat tea? Not fine.'

photos.location: /assets/articles/norwegian-getaway-aug-2026-trip/ (WebP, converted from operator's originals, max 1600px, q78)
photos.provenance: All five taken by the operator in his cabins on Day 1; verified against the images directly (captions describe only what is visible in each frame).
photos.contents_verified: 1) desk laminate edge chipped by storage cube + worn wastebasket; 2) trim veneer gouged to particleboard + debris embedded along carpet seam; 3) minifridge cabinet baseboard chipped/gouged with grit; 4) closet floor with previous guest's clear garment bag + pink wristband; 5) torn luggage-tag sticker ('REMOVE THIS PORTION ONLY') in carpet with debris flecks.

day_1_evening_addendum.fidelity_notes: Dirty-vs-deteriorated distinction (steward-fixable vs deferred maintenance) is editorial framing grounded in the photos, not a new factual claim. Hot-tub entry states ONLY the observed pattern (alcohol undisturbed; soda flagged; unsweet tea flagged) and explicitly disclaims knowledge of the policy logic; 'nobody profits from' line is analysis flagged as a reading to be tested during the week, not asserted fact. NOT claimed: who enforced, how many instances, whether cabins were fixed yet (still tomorrow's entry).

day_1_dining_and_engines.source: Ken's fourth in-session dispatch: O'Sheehan's lunch (fish and chips crunchy outside/moist inside; Irish Reuben lacked balance, too much acid); dinner NY strip + pair of lobster tails, verdict pending ('Will update you'); engines started and run off and on all evening.
day_1_dining_and_engines.dessert_and_thesis_source: Ken's sixth in-session dispatch: dessert = warm chocolate lava (cake) with cookies and cream gelato, raspberry coulis, mint leaf (no score dispatched — none printed); thesis verbatim basis: 'Even with the foibles its clear NCL had stepped up their food game.' Thesis printed in Ken's framing (foibles conceded, game stepped up); the foibles list in that sentence recaps only already-published Day 1 misses. 'Hits you don't get by accident' is editorial framing of the dispatched thesis. Compared-to-when NOT specified in print — the dispatch didn't say stepped up relative to which prior sailing.
day_1_dining_and_engines.dinner_verdict_source: Ken's fifth in-session dispatch: lobster 10/10 'yummy buttery perfections'; strip 8/10, 'would have been a 10 if it weren't over cooked'; cheese ravioli with lobster sauce good, seafood enjoyed but 'lobster wasn't singing as loudly as other notes' (kept nearly verbatim); ordered Greek salad, brought bruschetta, bruschetta 9/10 'excellent'. Scores exactly as dispatched. Closing line ('kitchen's mistake outscores your order') is editorial framing of the dispatched facts. Dinner venue still NOT named — never dispatched.
day_1_dining_and_engines.fidelity_notes: Venue name as the operator gave it (O'Sheehan's), linked to the existing venue page restaurants/ncl/osheehans.html. Dispatch typos normalized (nee york -> New York, lonster -> lobster, Ruben -> Reuben); '(oceans)' in the dispatch RESOLVED by operator follow-up: the name is verbal wordplay — O'Sheehan's said with an Irish accent sounds like 'oceans'. Written into the entry as how the name sounds, without attributing naming intent to NCL (unverified). Dinner venue NOT named (not dispatched); dinner verdict explicitly deferred. Engine entry states only the observation; both candidate explanations (pre-departure checks, ordinary hotel-load rhythm) offered as unknowns, no claim about whether shore power is connected. NOT claimed: times, which engines, exhaust, noise level in cabins.

day_1_underway_and_cabin_list.source: Ken's seventh in-session dispatch: (a) screenshot of the sailing's Facebook group (8:54 p.m. device time) — ship has left port; one passenger reports the shore-tie test succeeded so no need to stay in port ('casino could open' / 'no more sales tax' quip); another reports propulsion running below full force, ~7 knots slower; Ken's own group reply confirms the waiter said 'something technical with the engine that he didn't know about'; (b) two photos (Bremerhaven plaque, Getaway model); (c) 'our tv and door lock are broken. Maintenance is coming, apparently.'
day_1_underway_and_cabin_list.sourcing_discipline: Departure itself treated as fact (operator aboard, participating in the thread premise). ALL causal explanations printed as labeled scuttlebutt — 'passenger scuttlebutt, some of it secondhand from crew, none of it official'; fellow passengers NOT named on the site; the screenshot itself NOT published (other people's names/faces from a group). Engine-runs-were-the-test connection explicitly labeled 'a guess stacked on a rumor'. Shore-power verdict explicitly kept open pending better sourcing. The ~7-knots and shore-tie claims attributed to unnamed fellow passengers, not asserted.
day_1_underway_and_cabin_list.photos: day1-getaway-model.webp (model in glass case, hull art, abstract artwork behind — caption describes only what is visible); day1-bremerhaven-plaque.webp (rotated upright; plate legibly reads SEESTADT BREMERHAVEN; caption describes the relief and notes the ship was built in Germany — Getaway was built at Meyer Werft, already stated on our ship page — without claiming what the plaque commemorates).
day_1_underway_and_cabin_list.cabin_additions: TV broken, door lock broken, maintenance promised — 'apparently' kept as the operator's own skeptical word. Folded into the fix-it scorecard alongside cleaning.

day_1_ship_answered.source: Ken's eighth in-session dispatch: someone sent to vacuum; inside of the exterior door knob repaired; TV fixed; crew would 'note it in the report that the customer requested a dinner at the sushi restaurant for his mom' (quote as dispatched); Ken's analysis — low-hanging fruit, comped dinner guarantees a second purchased meal, gesture would be appreciated, 'But I doubt that will happen.'
day_1_ship_answered.vpn_note: Twelfth dispatch (Day 1): Tailscale blocked on the cheaper internet tier; traded up to the streaming tier which 'explicitly says vpn is enabled'; travel routers don't seem to work — a device behind a VPN-enabled travel router still hits the captive portal. Printed as dispatched. VERDICT RESOLVED by thirteenth dispatch: 'It does work on the upgraded tier, as does wireguard which is built on the same technology' — printed as: Tailscale works on the streaming tier, and so does plain WireGuard; relationship stated accurately in print (Tailscale is built on WireGuard, honoring the dispatch's same-technology point). Still NOT claimed: which protocols the cheaper tier blocks, or why. Cross-links the existing internet-at-sea.html guide.
day_1_ship_answered.ac_note: Eleventh dispatch (Day 1): 'air conditioner is nice and cool. All the way down was too cold. A pleasant surprise for me.' Printed as dispatched; the tie to the hot-day/no-breeze theme is framing on already-published facts.
day_1_ship_answered.anonymity_rule_scope: Tenth dispatch (2026-08-25) widened the rule to lifelong: 'I have always and will always hide my travel writer status from the cruise lines.' Intro updated from a this-week rule to 'the same rule that has governed every sailing I've ever written about.' Household memory 3dcdcd98 updated to permanent scope.
day_1_ship_answered.anonymity_rule: Ninth dispatch, verbatim basis: 'I did not and will not tell them I'm a travel writer. Keeps integrity high. If they won't do it for an average person. They won't do it for me either that way.' Printed twice: as a standing rule in the intro (governs the whole week) and as the terms-of-the-test paragraph after the sushi prediction (where the 'I'd write about it' line could otherwise be misread as something said to the crew). Both keep Ken's logic: anonymity means every response the ship makes is its average-guest response.
day_1_ship_answered.fidelity_notes: Same-night fixes stated as dispatched (vacuum, door handle, TV); 'apparently turned out to be unfair' is the honest walk-back of the earlier skepticism about response speed. Deeper-clean status NOT claimed — only a vacuum pass was dispatched, so the entry defers that to morning. Sushi venue NOT named (dispatch said 'the sushi restaurant'). The comp-economics analysis is Ken's own, printed in his framing; the doubt is printed as an explicit scored prediction the week can settle. 'I'd write about it' is inherent to the page's premise, not a new claim.

day_2_opening.source: Ken's first Day 2 dispatch (voice-dictated): breakfast orders right; poached eggs runny, over toast; family tradition of eggs poached in hot milk (northeastern comfort food via mother's family to Florida), improvised with poured hot milk, 'turned out fantastic'; salmon toast very good, light on salmon, 'beautiful even'; BOGO specialty-dining sale found, Wasabi booked tomorrow night; wheelchair observations.
day_2_opening.fidelity_notes: 'we walked to the ship' normalized to 'walked the ship' (voice-transcription artifact; they are aboard). Breakfast venue NOT named (not dispatched). Wasabi now named (dispatched); the tie-back to the sushi prediction is editorial but scoped — notes only that paying customers keep the prediction clean. 'Costs the ship almost nothing and changes that man's week' is editorial framing of Ken's stated respect.
day_2_opening.accessibility_claims: Hallway power-chair storage: stated as this sailing's observed accommodation (man in his 80s, no accessible cabin available). Pool/hot-tub policy (24h notice + exact minutes, lift not left deployed): attributed to 'some Norwegian ships, in our experience' per the dispatch, with 'appears to be the same way here' kept as appearance, not fact; 'I'm told they do exist' hedge kept verbatim in spirit. NOT claimed: NCL fleet-wide policy, this ship's written policy, ADA analysis. Cross-links existing accessibility.html and the Jewel lawsuit article (verified present).
day_2_opening.personal_anchor: Ken's care for people with disabilities earlier in his life — as dispatched.

day_2_room_meeting.source: Ken's second Day 2 dispatch: staff meeting about the room held in the room, 'Didn't feel heard'; maintenance re-sent for three doors (two squeaky, one bad lock); plans to fix busted trim; 'Timothy was great. Personable. Passionate about his job. He was the fixer.'; 'There are still toenails on my floor.'; 'Let's see what happens.'; irony — his comp request (book one, mother's comped) is basically the deal of the day / BOGO, booking Wasabi tomorrow night (typos normalized: 'ud for dijner st wasabi timirrje night' -> us for dinner at Wasabi tomorrow night).
day_2_room_meeting.fidelity_notes: 'Didn't feel heard' printed verbatim, no invented meeting details (attendees, content, tone all unknown — none written). Timothy named first-name-only exactly as dispatched, in praise — lived-grade crew mention per venue-page precedent. Toenails persistence printed against yesterday's vacuum visit (both facts already on page); 'the sentence I'd most like to delete' is editorial voice on the operator's fact. Irony paragraph connects the comp request to the already-published BOGO — 'bar for beating it just got lower' is editorial framing of Ken's own irony point. NOT claimed: whether the meeting produced decisions, who attended, why the vacuum missed the toenails.

day_2_lunch_spice_h2o.source: Ken's third Day 2 dispatch: room-service lunch — flank steak, Cobb salad, BLT. BLT excellent but small ('order two'); Cobb 6/10, chicken dry, requested balsamic vinaigrette missing, blue cheese choice fantastic; flank steak 8/10, overcooked but tender and moist, chimichurri fantastic. Then Spice H2O: hot tubs and pool full, found a shady table.
day_2_lunch_spice_h2o.fidelity_notes: Scores exactly as dispatched; typos normalized (thr/sidnt/baldamic/thst/gravbed/h20). Kitchen-pattern paragraph is editorial synthesis of facts already on the page (two overcooked steaks: Day 1 strip + Day 2 flank; two order-accuracy misses: bruschetta + vinaigrette; hits: chimichurri, blue cheese, Day 1 lobster '10/10 buttery perfection' recapped as 'buttery lobster') — 'good kitchen, loose execution' is the editorial reading of the operator's own scores. 'Ship underway' Tuesday afternoon grounded in the published itinerary (Nassau arrival Tuesday evening). Spice H2O linked to existing venue page. NOT claimed: which crew took the order, room-service wait time, Spice H2O crowding beyond full tubs/pool.

day_2_dinner.source: Ken's fourth Day 2 dispatch: bruschetta again 'once more fantastic'; spinach artichoke lacked seasoning, salt especially; parmesan-crusted pork chop salty and diminished by canned tomatoes on top; bluefish 10/10 flavorful, well balanced, wonderful; New England clam chowder THE standout — grandfather's family New England back to the early days (minutemen), grandmother (Floridian) learned their chowder, this gives it a run for its money; smoky, unctuous, flavorful; would benefit from a little spice (jalapenos); one of the best in decades, 'easily tied with my clam chowder experience in Alaska, and maybe better'; dessert update coming.
day_2_dinner.fidelity_notes: Typos normalized (thr/soinach/artchoke/tomatos/ithetwise/s little/updste). 'On purpose this time' is grounded in the published Day 1 accidental bruschetta. Salt-inconsistency observation (one dish under, one over, same course) is arithmetic on the dispatched verdicts, tied to the already-named loose-execution pattern. Family history printed close to verbatim — grandfather's NE line/minutemen, grandmother's learned chowder — no genealogical detail invented. Alaska chowder comparison kept as the operator's personal benchmark, no venue invented. Dinner venue still NOT named (not dispatched). 'Made it her own' is a light gloss on 'learned their chowder' + 'gives that a run for its money'.

day_2_dessert_and_evening.source: Ken's fifth Day 2 dispatch: dessert ordered = 'an 8o clock chocolate thing with a scoop of ice cream', received = two scoops of ice cream, 'Haha. More of the same.'; 90s pop-culture show — bright 'nickelodian'/'saved by the bell' colors, slightly campy vibe, referenced Friends, Blockbuster, Bop It, boy bands, 'All in all it was a good show'; comedy show after mediocre 'but at least didn't reuse the same six jokes every comedian on a ship tells.'
day_2_dessert_and_evening.fidelity_notes: Dessert name printed as 'a chocolate something' — the dispatch's own vagueness kept rather than guessing a menu name. 'Third order that came back different' is arithmetic on published misses (bruschetta, vinaigrette, dessert). Scratch-off framing matches Ken's laughing tone ('Haha'); no outrage. Show references and verdicts as dispatched; comedy line kept near-verbatim. Show names/venues NOT stated (not dispatched); typos normalized (ofnthe/nickelodian/block buster/st leadt didnt/comeddisnt).

day_2_toenail_resolution.source: Ken's sixth Day 2 dispatch: room steward returned, much better vacuum job, no toenails visible; 'Is it perfect? No. But it is acceptable now.'; rhetorical q verbatim: 'What is the acceptable number of toenails? On a luxury cruise?'; free load of laundry offered, 'So thats something ar least.'
day_2_toenail_resolution.fidelity_notes: Resolution and perfect/acceptable verdict printed as dispatched. ONE deliberate departure, flagged for operator review: the rhetorical 'On a luxury cruise?' printed as 'On a cruise?' — dropped 'luxury' because NCL Getaway is not classified a luxury line and the site's precision standard outweighs the rhetorical flourish; Ken can restore his word if he prefers the sting. Monday-to-Tuesday timeline is page arithmetic. Laundry comp printed with Ken's lukewarm register ('So that's something, at least'); explicitly separated from the still-open sushi prediction so the wager stays scoreable.

day_3_breakfast.source: Ken's first Day 3 dispatch: Belgian waffles, steak and eggs (two over easy), fruit bowl, side of bacon. Waffles very good + blueberry syrup; eggs nice runny yolks; fruit fresh/ripe/nice presentation; steak cooked appropriately; bacon never came; waffles were cold.
day_3_breakfast.fidelity_notes: All verdicts as dispatched, including the deliberate contradiction (waffles very good AND cold — both kept). 'First win of the doneness column' and 'fourth order to arrive different' are arithmetic on published events (overcooked strip Day 1, overcooked flank Day 2 lunch -> appropriate steak Day 3; bruschetta, vinaigrette, dessert, now bacon). 'Last stretch between pan and plate' is editorial synthesis of the three-day pattern (originally phrased with a figurative distance; reworded number-free — an unsourced number, even as idiom, reads as a measurement on this site). Venue NOT named (not dispatched). Ship location NOT stated — Nassau arrival hasn't been dispatched, so the entry doesn't place the ship. Freshness stamps bumped to 2026-08-26 and ai-summary refreshed per standing obligation.

day_3_nassau_wasabi.source: Ken's second Day 3 dispatch: wandered Nassau, saw the Queen's Staircase and walked down from the top, shopping in port, conch fritters; back to ship, nap; Wasabi dinner outstanding, 'Start to finish everything was a 10. Including jewel our waitress who took great care of us.'
day_3_nassau_wasabi.photos_added: Third Day 3 dispatch ('Some photos from the day'): five operator photos -> WebP day3-*.webp (carriage and plaque rotated upright; verified visually). Contents verified against the images: staircase gorge from above; steps + waterfall with visitors; interpretive plaque (legible); horse-drawn surrey at Shirley Street light; Nassau Public Library sign. Crowd photos are public-place travel photography per Quantum embarkation-line precedent; no one identified in captions.
day_3_nassau_wasabi.queens_staircase_history_source: PRIMARY SOURCE — the on-site interpretive plaque, photographed legibly by the operator and published on the page. Facts printed are ONLY the plaque's, attributed in text ('here is what it says'): named for Queen Victoria (queen 1837); chiselled from solid limestone circa 1830s by free men of African descent; 'The 66 Steps'; remains of a stone quarry; 31m tall; public access between Fort Fincastle and the city; paving reduced count to 64; 'symbol of resilience' quote. NO training-data history added and no adjudication beyond the plaque — the page quotes the site's own telling.
day_3_nassau_wasabi.fidelity_notes: Nassau activities exactly as dispatched — no Queen's Staircase history/step-count added from memory (the earlier restraint), now superseded ONLY by the plaque photo as source (port page still carries the guide content; cross-linked). Jewel named first-name-only in praise per crew-mention pattern (capitalized from the dispatch's lowercase). 'No asterisks tonight' is editorial framing of the all-10s verdict against the page's own prior scores. Prediction handling: tonight was the self-booked BOGO, so the promised-gesture prediction is explicitly kept OPEN and unscored — the entry says so rather than letting the BOGO read as the ship's gesture. NOT claimed: what was ordered at Wasabi (not dispatched), conch fritter venue, Nassau repair-berth observations (not dispatched).

day_1_heat_note.source: Ken's third in-session dispatch, verbatim basis: 'No breeze on a cruise ship that's not moving. It's hot in South Florida today.'
day_1_heat_note.fidelity_notes: Dispatched facts: no breeze while stationary; hot in South Florida today. Apparent-wind framing (deck breeze is mostly the ship's own motion) is general physics, stated generically with no wind-speed numbers. 'Small hours' departure defers to the already-published, letter-sourced ~3 a.m. departure in the Day 1 morning entry. The trade-off framing (port-heavy itinerary trades away underway evenings) is editorial, tied to the published itinerary change. NOT claimed: deck temperatures, AC performance, whether shore power is connected tonight (that remains the owed shore-power report).

day_4_gsc_and_moderno.source: Ken's Day 4 dispatches across several messages: 'Last full day: largely good. Bad experience at Modernos.'; pier open, temporary while permanent is built, long walk, 'Everything isn't fully accessible but it's better than other islands'; two photographed signs; 'They changed schedule again, we left port around 6 I think'; 'Never saw a lift deployed, talked to a person in a chair that was satisfied with the handicap accommodations but can't swim won't do hot tubs'; 'They never did follow through and tonight at Moderna made it worse'; Moderno detail ($16 pending credit, $2.75 pending charge, cash account, card 'closed', held in restaurant, hour to eat + hour chasing the bill, left for luggage with fifteen minutes to spare, waiter yelling after him about a 'financing issue'); operator's own chosen phrasing 'the employees were rude with an elderly woman in my own family to the point of tears'; Hristina escalation, apology, write-up and retraining promise, offer declined ('nothing... its the last day... we might not be back. lets see'); third billing error (two charges for one photo); 'NCL wants you to prepay. the beverage package is always the first thing to be taken'; 'Missing the fleetwood mac tribute concert hurt my moms heart too. she loves that band.'

primary_sources.zipline_requirements: PHOTOGRAPHED SIGN — age 8 min / under-18 accompanied; 50-250 lb (23-113 kg); 4 ft / 122 cm; dress code; 'able to climb a 20-foot ladder unassisted' quoted verbatim; closed-toe/heel-strap footwear naming Crocs and Keens; not-recommended conditions list. Published as day4-gsc-zipline-safety-rules-sign.webp.

day_4_gsc_and_moderno.pier_resolution: The published GSC article printed the reopening as an unresolved conflict between sources and promised this sailing would settle it. Settled: open, temporary, permanent under construction. Recorded here; the GSC article itself is NOT yet updated (separate task).
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.uncertainty_preserved: Departure time printed as 'around 6, though I'm going from memory and not a printed time, so treat that figure as unconfirmed' — Ken said 'I think'. The 8 a.m.-8 p.m. island call is attributed to NCL's pre-sailing itinerary-change letter, the source our earlier articles used, and the entry says only that we left earlier than that.
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.lift_question: Deliberately left OPEN. The wheelchair user Ken spoke with was satisfied but does not swim or use hot tubs, so his answer does not address lift deployment; the entry says so explicitly and refuses to close the question with an unrelated yes. Four days, no lift seen deployed — stated as observation, not as proof of policy.
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.prediction_scored: Monday's printed prediction (ship would not follow through on the sushi dinner for his mother) resolved AGAINST the ship. Scored in text without triumph; the BOGO the family paid for is explicitly distinguished from the promised gesture.
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.naming_policy: Hristina named (first name only, as dispatched, in praise for handling the escalation). The employees NOT named — operator's own phrasing is plural and anonymous, and the entry states the reasoning: the training failure belongs to the ship, and an indexed page is the wrong instrument for a line-level worker. This sets the site's rule for negative crew encounters.
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.pastoral_handling: The mother is described exactly as Ken chose to describe her ('an elderly woman in my own family'), never named. Her tears are stated once, plainly, with 'no version of that sentence I can soften' rather than dramatised. The declined compensation is printed because it proves the page was not written to extract anything. The missed Fleetwood Mac tribute closes the section as the real cost, without editorial embellishment.
day_4_gsc_and_moderno.not_claimed: Which restaurant staff member did what; what Hristina's role or title is; whether the retraining happened; the exact departure time; the exact luggage deadline; the concert's performer names beyond 'Fleetwood Mac tribute'; any pricing for Great Tides Waterpark or Great Life Lagoon (still unverified — the zipline board was the pricing Ken photographed, and the entry does not let it stand in for the waterpark question).

day_5_disembarkation.source: Ken's Day 5 dispatch: disembarkation quick, easy, orderly; they dragged their feet and were among the last off; breakfast a little chaotic 'but no more so than you would expect on the last day in the main dining room'; after disembarking picked up hot pressed Cubans and picnicked in the Everglades; a pavilion over the water that usually has a good breeze and rocking chairs; thoroughly enjoyed it.
day_5_disembarkation.fidelity_notes: All as dispatched. Breakfast chaos explicitly NOT counted against the ship, matching Ken's own framing. The bookend observation (boarding smooth Monday, disembarkation smooth Friday, failures concentrated in cabin/table/folio) is arithmetic on already-published entries. Everglades location NOT named beyond 'the Everglades' and the pavilion NOT named — the dispatch didn't, so the page doesn't. 'Usually has a good breeze' kept as the dispatch's own hedge. The callback to Day 1's no-breeze note is internal cross-reference, not a new claim.
day_5_disembarkation.verdict_status: The week verdict is DEFERRED in text on purpose — the page says it will be written with distance rather than in the parking lot. Not an omission; a stated commitment.

week_verdict.source: Ken's verdict dispatch: 'They are making great strides verse [versus] where they were before Covid with improvements in shows and food. But their lack of attention to detail and Norwegian first customer service policies continue to weigh them down. I have not decided if I'll be back or not. For sure my mother wont.'
week_verdict.fidelity_notes: Ken's three-part thesis printed in his structure and order: strides first (credit before criticism), then the two weights, then the undecided/decided split. 'Norwegian first customer service policies' read as policies serving Norwegian before the customer and rendered as 'customer-service policies that put Norwegian first' — his coinage preserved. 'verse' normalized to 'versus'/'against'. Pre-Covid comparison is Ken's own from prior sailings; NO invented detail about what NCL was like pre-Covid. Every supporting item recaps already-published page facts (four order errors, cabin arc, three billing errors, the $2.75 card lock, prepay/beverage-package mechanic, the unkept report promise, Timothy/Jewel/Hristina). Mother's decision limited to Norwegian, not cruising generally — the dispatch said 'be back'. NOT claimed: that she was a longtime NCL customer, any loyalty tier, or that Ken has ruled Norwegian out.
week_verdict.editorial_additions: The crew-vs-policy distinction ('a company can rewrite a policy in an afternoon; it takes years to build a crew worth defending') and the closing line ('The kitchen isn't what they need to fix') are mine, built only on published page facts — flagged here as editorial, not dispatched.
